steps.text: Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add orzo; cook and stir until orzo is golden brown.
Stir in onion and cook until onion becomes translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in rice and chicken broth, turn heat to high, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover the skillet, and simmer until rice is tender and liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sarah’s Rice Pilaf
raw_recipe.description: This rice pilaf brings together nutty orzo pasta, aromatic onion and garlic, and chicken broth for super flavor. An easy, delicious, anytime side.

video.description: In this video you’ll see how to make a side dish with orzo pasta and rice. We’ll first cook the pasta in butter with onion and garlic to get a nice toasty flavor. Then, add the rice and simmer in chicken broth. Try using vegetable broth to make this vegetarian.

review.reviewBody: When I first decided to make this recipe, I was little dubious because the ingredients didn't seem too exciting. Boy, was I wrong! This dish was incredibly good...something that I would definitely make again! The taste/texture was similar to Rice-a-Roni, but so much better, without that packaged taste. I topped it with chopped chives for a little more color, and everyone loved it. Thanks so much for sharing!!!

When I made this recipe, I found it to be a little, O.K., alot bland. But, I did use homemade chicken broth, and while very tasty, it was not overly salted. Perhaps using store bought broth would be more flavorful. I followed the recipe exactly, and I did feel the measurements are spot-on. It makes enough for four people, and the liquid ratio is perfect with the dry ingredients. Once I salted at the stove and the table, I found this to be a really tasty side dish I plan to serve again.

We liked it but the order you add ingredients seems off to me. I've made other pilafs and always start with the onion because that takes longest to cook. After the onion softens then I added the rice and orzo and when those were almost done toasting I added the garlic for a couple minutes, then the broth. But the proportions were good.

You cannot get any easier than this and the best part is that it is absolutely delicious. This is 100x better than any boxed rice can be. The only thing I added was a little salt, because of the low sodium broth I used. I also don't measure the onion, just chopped half of a big onion and threw it in. It pairs quite well with roasted chicken and butternut squash. Thanks for the delicious recipe!

My husband and I both loved this recipe. I added half a green pepper like one of the other reviewers suggested, but other than that I followed the recipe exactly and it was perfect! Thanks for sharing!!
Absolutely delicious! I steamed some broccoli, chopped it up finely, and tossed that into the pilaf. Outstanding! It's a very flexible side dish that would go well with just about any meal!

I've made this twice now and we really like it. After reading the ingredient list on the Uncle Ben's Rice Pilaf box, I added a little turmeric the second time I made it. Of course I didn't add the msg that was also listed! It is very easy to make and is moist and flavorful! Thank you, Sarah!

This recipe was a great start.

I started by sautéing finely chopped onions in the butter, then adding the orzo and minute rice, sautéing them until toasted. I then added the garlic and stirred.

Next, I added low-sodium chicken broth, pepper, thyme, and a bit of fresh squeezed lemon juice (which gives the flavor a lift). I actually grated a bit of parmesean into it, but it's not necessary. I was fixing the rice along with pan-fried sea bass, so that sounded good. 

Note: If you add cheese, just watch the pan so it doesn't scorch. 

I added fresh, finely chopped parsley, then stirred until it began to set up. I transferred it to a microwave-safe bowl, covered it with plastic wrap, then let it sit until my fish and veggies were done, then I cooked it covered for two minutes to warm it back up. I uncovered it, fluffed it with a fork, and served. 

It was delicious! I gave the recipe 4, instead of 5, stars because I believe the modifications I made improved the recipe as written.

The rice and orzo were cooked perfectly with this recipe but it lacked basic seasoning. Author needs to include salt & pepper amounts. 2nd make: used low sodium chicken broth, added 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, sprinkles of Mrs. Dash. wouldn't use pepper or Mrs. Dash next time, maybe use Herbamare salt. 3rd make: Use 2 c water + 2 tsp chicken bouillon for the broth. Better flavor. Maybe add onion powder next time. 3rd time is the charm: let the orzo get really brown, used a sweet onion, low sodium chicken broth and 3/4 tsp. Herbamare seasoning.

Great recipe and so much healthier than the boxed pilaf. I added 1/4 tsp. turmeric, 1/4 tsp. paprika and 2 tsp. parsley. This will definitely become a staple in our household. I did not add any salt so the only sodium came from the chicken broth.

A great staple around our house! Just a few suggestions though... 1) Add 1/2 tsp dried thyme and a 1/2 tsp dried basil when mixing in the rice and broth. 2) My store sometimes runs out of orzo and I use "Cut Fideo #1" and it works fine. 3) I cook ahead of time, doubling the recipe, then after it cools spoon it into 4-5 freezer baggies and freeze it. When you need quick rice pilaf, take a baggie out, heat it in the microwave 3 minutes and presto!
Tasty served with halibut.
Made exactly as written. Quick, easy and tasty side to a rack of BBQ ribs!
I made it as listed. Easy and very tasty! I will be making this more often going forward.
I like rice pilaf as a different side dish.
I had run out of garlic so I had to omit with some cumin .

Good method for pilaf, but not enough flavor for my taste. Not bad. Bland. First, there is no salt in the recipe. What? Rice without salt? Please. I added salt, chicken bouillon powder, green onion, parsley, and slivered almonds. This will be a good base, and I’ll keep playing with it til I get it right.
I never made rice like this, it was very good. Will definitely make again.
Recommend

I have had a similar rice that was made by an Iranian woman. She used a lot of Cumin seed during the sautéing of the orzo, onion and garlic. I added about a tablespoon for half the recipe. I’m still cooking the rice so I will have to see how it turns out. But I recommend that you try the cumin seed in your rice recipes.
